title: The decision code of an agent step and the placement and key set of the agent run, the mode, the fallback and its reason are in no source
source: RWB-TE-013 sections 4, 7, 8 and 12; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2.4.2, A2.2.4.3 and A2.3.4.3
description: The legacy story maps the entry as case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, agent_version, model_version, inputs_ref, recommendation, final_call and actions holding agentRunId, mode, fallback and fallbackReason, and gives no list of decision codes. TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives decision_log_entry a decision_code from LOV-DECISION and an actions jsonb, and T3.2 does not enumerate LOV-DECISION; no source states which code or sub-decision an agent step carries, nor which of the remaining entry fields holds the agent run id, the mode, the fallback and its reason.
evidence: RWB-TE-013 section 12 (Decision log mapping and the actions key list) and AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC8; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003, -009, -012, -014 and -031; T3.2 lists LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-PRODUCT only; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-05 refuses an unknown decision code with no list published.
proposed: Carry the decision code in force from LOV-DECISION, put the agent run id, the mode, the fallback and its reason in actions as the legacy mapping does, keep recommendation and final_call as separate fields, and settle the code of an agent step with the reference-data owner before the first joint environment.

title: The text of MSG-P7-009 and the identifiers and texts of the not-found answer and the chain-break report are not written in any source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.4.4, A2.2.4.2, A2.2.4.3 and A2.5.4.3; RWB-TE-013 sections 5 and 14; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.2
description: The FSD names MSG-P7-009 as the message of a record refused at the schema check, and the 404 and the same-day chain-break report as outcomes, without writing their text or allocating an id to the last two. Section 14 therefore carries two messages with a written text and two outcomes whose id and text stand as the placeholder.
evidence: FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 (refused with MSG-P7-009 naming the field, text not written); AC-BG-P7-001-01 and AC-BG-P7-002-01 (a break is reported the same day, report text and id absent); TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 gives 404 without a message; RWB-TE-013 section 14 lists MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P4-002 only.
proposed: Write the text of MSG-P7-009 once with the P7 business analyst, keep it as the carrier of the decision-code, rule-version, agent-version, inputs-reference and decided-time refusals, and keep the legacy field names inside it character for character.

title: The platform build dependencies, the authorise answer and the agent contract that the patterns add are not in the metadata rows, and RWB-P10-TE013-CON is not written
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; P7 context pack; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (P4 rows)
description: The eleven decoupling patterns add seven platform contract stories as build dependencies (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON), one cross-service contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and, for the two reads, the authorise answer of rwb-access through the platform guard, while the story line fixes the build dependency as empty and the contract dependency as RWB-P10-TE013-CON alone. The Ownership Map has no authorise operation row, and the agent contract that the entry is validated against is not yet published.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19; R5.7 rules 2, 3 and 8; Ownership Map v1 P4 rows (role, permission, masking_rule, delegation_limit) with no authorise path; the story line of WP B2-P7-007 with H empty and C RWB-P10-TE013-CON.
proposed: Treat the seven platform contracts and RWB-P3-E1043-CON as wave 0 and contract fakes, treat the authorise answer as the platform guard the reads declare, keep the metadata rows as the Work Package fixes them, and replace the agent contract fake with RWB-P10-TE013-CON when it lands.

title: The per-service login name, the environment and property names and the time of the chain check are in no source
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02 and DP-10; P7 context pack; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.4.4; RWB-TE-013 section 13
description: The patterns fix one login and one Schedule per service and the sources fix neither the login name, nor the consumer group, the environment names, the migration user and the property names of the service, nor the time of day, timezone and overlap policy of the nightly chain check that covers these entries.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02 and DP-10 and the P7 context pack service row; TSD P7 v2 T6.2 (service identities) with no login name; FSD P7 v3 AC-BG-P7-001-01 (nightly, break reported the same day) with no time; RWB-TE-013 section 13 names only the feature flag rwb.agent.client, which is the client's and not this story's.
proposed: Take the login, the consumer group, the Flyway user and the property names from the service template and the platform DB story, and take the chain-check time from the decision-log store slice, which owns JOB-14.

title: The model version of agent INTAKE is named in no source
source: RWB-TE-013 sections 4, 7, 11 and 12; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1
description: The legacy story records the model version on the entry as the value the run names and never fixes a literal, and no source in this Work Package names the model version of agent INTAKE, so the tests can only assert equality with the run fixture.
evidence: RWB-TE-013 section 12 (model_version from the run) and section 11 (DF-DEC-006 read from the run); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-006 model_version varchar(40) with source COLLINS and no value.
proposed: Assert equality between the entry and the run fixture rather than a literal, and publish the model version of each live agent with the agent policy in the rwb-agent contract.

title: The legacy story says the client publishes no event while DP-03 requires the record on the shared decision-record topic
source: RWB-TE-013 section 12 (Events) and section 4; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T5.3
description: The legacy story fixes that the agent client publishes no event and that the decision log is written through the P7 writer inside one monolith, while the target writes the record locally through the DP-03 library and publishes DecisionRecorded on the shared topic that this service collects. TSD P7 v2 T5.3 lists DecisionRecorded as a published event of the module, which supports the topic reading; the legacy sentence and the pattern disagree.
evidence: RWB-TE-013 section 12 (Events: EV-28 is published by the orchestrator; the client publishes none); TSD P7 v2 T5.3 (DecisionRecorded, published); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and R3 source precedence, where the pattern and the architecture outrank the story master.
proposed: Take the DP-03 reading: the calling service appends the record locally in its own schema and transaction and publishes DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 from its outbox, and this service collects it into the ledger; the legacy sentence is superseded and no event comes from the client of rwb-agent.

title: The fixed story path already held an artefact of the superseded Work Package B-P7-05 whose citations resolve to no register row
source: status.json (B-P7-05 SUPERSEDED, stopped for the B2 split queue); the file at the fixed path before this Work Package; the split plan
description: The story path fixed by this Work Package was occupied by a 73,677-byte file of the same story key written for Work Package B-P7-05, which status.json records as SUPERSEDED. That artefact cited CG-B-P7-05-TE013-1 to -6 and ASM-B-P7-05-TE013-1 to -7, and no row with those ids exists in the gap or assumption registers, so the citations resolved to nothing and the story catalogue fragment would have stayed inconsistent with the registers.
evidence: status.json entry B-P7-05 SUPERSEDED with the note 'stopped for the B2 split queue'; the citation strings of the earlier artefact; the absence of every CG-B-P7-05-TE013 and ASM-B-P7-05-TE013 id from _work/msr/gaps and _work/msr/assumptions.
proposed: Replace the artefact at the fixed path in full, carry its substance forward, and cite only rows written by this Work Package; a v2 copy would itself be a path outside the Write only block.

title: The fallback-rate measure, its operation name and its threshold ownership are in no source
source: RWB-TE-013 section 2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.1 and A2.1.4.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17
description: The legacy story sets the agent fallback rate below 10 percent per month and names no operation, no parameters and no owner of the definition, and the target removes the data lake and moves reporting to events, so the measure is read from another service while its definition is owned elsewhere. No source states the query, the period grain, the rounding or the service that publishes the measure.
evidence: RWB-TE-013 section 2 (measure: agent fallback rate, target below 10 percent per month); FSD P7 v3 A2.1.1 and A2.1.4.3 (decision-log metric with no agent rate); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 (no data lake; reporting from events into rwb-reporting).
proposed: Keep the threshold below 10 percent per month with rwb-reporting as the definition owner, make the count by agent version and month readable from the ledger, and leave the operation name and the period grain to the reporting contract.

title: The EV number of the DecisionRecorded event is left open by the Ownership Map among three P7 events
source: P7 context pack (events EV-08, EV-09, EV-30); TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T5.3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
description: The context pack lists three events owned by P7 without their names and TSD P7 v2 T5.3 names only DecisionRecorded and ApprovalRequested, so no source in this Work Package ties DecisionRecorded to one of EV-08, EV-09 or EV-30.
evidence: P7 context pack Ownership rows, Events (3): EV-08, EV-09, EV-30; TSD P7 v2 T5.3 (DecisionRecorded and ApprovalRequested, published); Ownership Map v1 with no event-to-name table in the pack.
proposed: Publish the event under the name rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 and tie it to the P7 event row when the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog v1 is indexed, without changing the topic or the payload.
